slot_note: re-root of task130 after the v1 portal failure (both top models filed the golden); same slot, same domain and subdomain, new graded quantity and a methodological stump
niche: a borough council's temporary-accommodation team sizing the replacement units it must call off, by bedroom size, for the homeless households still in a leased block on the day the owner takes it back, when those households leave only as move-on offers reach them
answer: Call off 46 replacement units for 1 April 2027: no one-bed, 7 two-bed, 20 three-bed and 19 four-bed.
answer_source: task130/submission.md, 1. Final Recommendation (the Call-off sheet of golden/tenter_house_replacement_units.xlsx carries the same units)
stakeholder_role: temporary accommodation and procurement manager at a borough council, who puts the replacement-unit call-off to the cabinet member for housing

spine.entity: one temporary-accommodation placement of one homeless household (a household's stay runs across one or more placements)

world.org_type: borough council housing needs service with a temporary-accommodation portfolio of leased blocks, private-sector leases and nightly-paid units

driver: Members of a closed group leave only when a rationed supply reaches them, and the supply is handed out across a wider list in a filed priority order within each size class, so how many remain at a later date is each member's rank inside its class against the cumulative planned supply, and neither a leaving rate nor a survival curve read off history, which both average over whatever list length the past happened to have, gives it.
driver_concrete: Tenter House takes no new placements after the owner's notice, and a household on the main duty leaves temporary accommodation only when a move-on offer reaches it; offers go to every main-duty household in the borough, wherever it lives, in order of the date the duty was accepted within each bedroom size, against the monthly numbers in the move-on plan, so the households still in the block on 31 March 2027 are those whose place in their size's list lies beyond the plan's offers, near the front for some sizes and far back for others.
stump: A competent solver rebuilds each household's stay from its placements, measures how fast main-duty households have been leaving temporary accommodation over the last year by bedroom size (or fits a survival curve on time since the duty was accepted, or shares the plan's lets out over the borough's list) and runs the Tenter House households forward on it, calling off around 136 units; the step that lands it there is forecasting departures as a rate, when after its first months a household leaves only when a move-on let reaches it, lets go borough-wide in duty-date order within each bedroom size against the move-on plan, and Tenter House's households sit near the front of those lists because its flats have gone to the longest-waiting nightly-paid household since 2023, so most of them are reached before 31 March: the queue leaves 46 households (no one-bed, 7 two-bed, 20 three-bed, 19 four-bed).

differentiation.task80: task80 dates a fixed-term status from the criterion event that conferred it rather than from when it was first observed operating; here nothing is dated or certified: a closed group's departures are a rank inside a borough-wide priority list against a planned supply, read per size class, and the wrong readings are rates and survival curves, not a mis-dated status.
differentiation.task86: task86 files the list order and works it as a low rung; its decisive move is an earlier hidden draw on the same pool that empties the front of the list. Here the list order itself is the decisive rung, filed nowhere and recovered only from the lets log, and nothing draws on the supply before the list.
differentiation.task50: task50 shares a component (a supply worked against demand) on a different driver; here departures from a closed group are a rank inside a borough-wide list against planned lets, which no rate or curve reproduces.
differentiation.task125: task125 sizes a council call-off for April 2027 too (shape 02, purchase order, local government), but its driver is unrelated; the deliverable stem was renamed from calloff_2027 to replacement_units so the two do not share a file name.

lineage.fate: failed on the portal 2026-10-10: both top models filed the golden seven-section designation
lineage.driver: The committed set is read off holdings on a future effective date built forward from a past snapshot of filed returns; the forward roll, with a third party's takeovers of scheduled transfers completed on the fixed interval its settled cases show, reproduces both closed controls because every holder enrolled by the snapshot had filed, but the holder population on the effective date also takes in holders enrolled after the snapshot who have not filed yet, whose units are recoverable only by grouping the transfer extract on the buyer, so a unit the roll leaves under the threshold is over it.

notes: Re-rooted after the v1 portal failure. The v1 world (large-holder designation from ownership returns) had no analytic stump left: every surviving idea was a hidden record a diligent solver joins or a unit swap the judge reads as a lens flip. The re-root keeps the domain and subdomain and moves to a methodological stump: a closed group's departures forecast as a rank inside a rationed priority list rather than as a rate. stump_strategy 'other': the decisive property is the allocation order (a rank inside a group against a cumulative planned supply), not a limit that removes the natural pick, so binding_constraint (task127, task128) is not the move; the supply limit is common to every reading and the rate readings already respect it.
